input.question: Why do employers reject applicants on the basis that they are overqualified?
input.ground_truth: Because an overqualified person is more likely to leave. It costs money to find, hire and train an employee. Someone who is overqualified for a position is likely to be looking for a higher paying job that better suits their qualifications. Why invest money and time into someone who is likely to leave.

Now, your mom says, “Let’s make simple chocolate chip cookies together!” But because you already know *so* much, you start telling her all the fancy ways to make the cookies and want to change the recipe to something really complicated.

Your mom might feel like you don’t really want to just help her with the simple cookies. She might think, “Oh, maybe she wants to do it her own way, or maybe she doesn’t want to listen to me.” So, sometimes, even if you’re really good, grown-ups (like bosses) might say, “No thank you,” because they think you might not want to do the simple job the way they want, or you might get bored and leave soon.

That’s why sometimes, even if someone knows a lot, they might not get the job—they are called “overqualified,” and the boss thinks it might not be a good fit.
